kernel.title: Knowledge lapse works as a change oracle: an inspect-tier field vanishes exactly when its hidden value changes; fractions keep their knowledge across 0.5 absolute drift
kernel.owner: kernel realism (Knowledge.level)
kernel.repro: Script: scratchpad/hv/p8_lapse.py, built on make_house(3,1,3), seed=0. cab_9 has locked=False; bucket_9 has fill_level 0.62. Unseen events: at_step 7 set entities.cab_9.locked=True; at step 8 set bucket fill to 0.20; at step 11 set it to 0.11. Steps: approach + inspect the cabinet, approach + inspect the bucket, then repeated env.step('wait') while watching the glance records.
kernel.evidence: cab.locked shows False through step 6. At step 7, exactly when the unseen lock happened, the field becomes <absent>. For a boolean this tells the agent the new value (now locked) without trying or inspecting. Bucket: inspected at 0.6, then shows 0.2 at inspect precision after an unseen drop of 0.42, with no re-inspection, because the tolerance is max(0.5, 2%). It turns into the bucket 'low' at step 11, which tells the agent the value has just crossed 0.62-0.5.
kernel.fix: When a known value changes, do not stop showing the field. Keep showing the last-learned value (marked stale with an age) until re-perceived, or degrade uniformly every N seconds whether or not the value changed. Replace the absolute 0.5 tolerance with a per-field instrument tolerance (fractions ~0.02-0.05, temperature ~0.3 C, etc.).

navigation_robot.title: No-tool 'measure method=estimate' and 'check_level' eyeball redraw their error every step; averaging recovers hidden tool-only geometry to tape and level precision
navigation_robot.repro: Script: scratchpad/hv/p9_estimates.py, built on make_house(3,1,3), seed=3. sofa_9 has size_m [2.0,0.9,0.8] and hidden _extents_mm [2043,917,846]. shelf_9 has hidden _tilt_deg [0.37,-0.22]. Steps: env.step('approach', sofa), then 40 x env.step('measure', sofa, dimension='dims', method='estimate'). Then env.step('approach', shelf), then 60 x env.step('check_level', shelf) holding no level.
navigation_robot.evidence: Single estimates scatter about +-8% (e.g. [1950,980,790] and [2130,870,890]). The error magnitude is drawn from U(3%,8%) with a random sign, so readings are never within 3% of the truth. Estimating T = (min(high)/1.03 + max(low)/0.97)/2 gives 2044.9 / 919.9 / 845.0 against hidden 2043 / 917 / 846. Inverting E[round(t+U(-0.8,0.8))] over the integer eyeball readings gives tilt 0.37 / -0.20 against hidden 0.37 / -0.22, which beats the spirit level's 0.1-degree resolution. Cause: the rng is ctx.rng = Random(seed:step:action), so it changes every step.
navigation_robot.fix: Key the no-tool errors on (seed, target, dimension, robot cell) and not on the step, so repeating from the same spot gives the same reading (the kernel's 'no free averaging' rule). Use a continuous zero-centred error (e.g. gauss) without the +-3% dead zone that brackets the truth. Optionally cap repeats from distinct viewpoints, or quantize estimates to 5 cm before adding noise.
